_doc: copy this folder to the Jetson; placeholders marked
_cmd_per_mps_doc: PLACEHOLDER -- replace with the real steady-state cmd-vs-speed slope from the calibration campaign (or point calibration_file at a fitted calibration JSON instead).
_erpm_per_mps_doc: PLACEHOLDER -- electrical RPM per m/s, used to convert VESC-reported erpm into v_now/v_est. Replace with the real motor/gearing/wheel-radius-derived value (or the calibration file's own fitted value, which overrides this when calibration_file is set).
_watchdog_ms_doc: Driver v2: raised from the pre-v2 default of 250ms -- 250ms proved too tight against real ackermann-stream jitter/latency on the actual robot, causing spurious watchdog brakes; 1500ms gives real-world margin while still being a small fraction of a human's reaction time.

kick._kick_duty_doc: actuation=="governor" only -- raw duty the kick bypass emits instead of kick_cmd (kick_cmd/kick_erpm_threshold are erpm-flavored and don't apply to a duty-only governor). See src/DriverCore.h's KickConfig.

_command_semantics_doc: "accel" (default, unchanged pre-v2 behavior: wire accel is integrated into v_target, wire speed ignored) | "velocity" (wire speed IS the target, wire accel is repurposed as a slew-rate bound). See src/DriverCore.h's CommandSemantics.
_actuation_doc: "map" (default -- legacy LinearMap/CalibratedMap path via calibration_file, unchanged pre-v2 behavior) | "governor" (SpeedGovernor + velocity_calib-based VelocityMap, duty-only output). See src/DriverCore.h's ActuationMode. velocity_calib/steering_angle_map files are resolved by vesc_driver_main.cpp's own CLI/$HOME/.vesc precedence, not driver_config.json keys -- see README.md.
_wheel_base_doc: meters -- cross-checked against a loaded steering_angle_map's own wheel_base at startup (mismatch is a hard, nonzero-exit error).
_default_slew_mps2_doc: command_semantics=="velocity" only -- default/held slew bound (m/s^2) before the first finite wire-accel value ever arrives.

governor._doc: actuation=="governor" only -- see src/SpeedGovernor.h. max_duty is NOT configurable here; it always comes from safety.max_duty above.
